outline: 1133 Area of a Triangle using Trigonometry

examples.question_text: Solve $x^{2}=5^{2}+8^{2}-2(5)(8)\cos60^{\circ}$ for the positive value of $x$.

examples.solution_text:
The $60^{\circ}$ angle is between the two known sides; $x$ is opposite it.
$\begin{aligned}c^{2}&=a^{2}+b^{2}-2ab\cos C\\x^{2}&=7^{2}+10^{2}-2(7)(10)\cos60^{\circ}\\x&=\sqrt{79}\\x&\approx8.89\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

Let $x$ be the third side. The given angle is the included angle.
$\begin{aligned}c^{2}&=a^{2}+b^{2}-2ab\cos C\\x^{2}&=180^{2}+120^{2}-2(180)(120)\cos120^{\circ}\\x&=\sqrt{68400}\\x&\approx262\text{ m}\end{aligned}$
Since $\cos120^{\circ}=-\frac12$, the cosine term adds to the sum of the squares.

$\begin{aligned}HJ^{2}&=9^{2}+12^{2}-2(9)(12)\cos60^{\circ}\\HJ&=\sqrt{117}\text{ cm}\\P&=9+12+\sqrt{117}\\P&\approx31.8\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$
Use the unrounded third side when calculating the perimeter.

examples.derivation: cos 60° = 1/2, so x² = 25 + 64 − 40 = 49. The requested positive root is x = 7. This adapts the supplied-equation exercise at lines 785–790; no diagram is required.

x² = 49 + 100 − 140(1/2) = 79, giving x = 8.888194… cm ≈ 8.89 cm. The diagram has AB:AC = 7:10, angle BAC = 60°, and x opposite that angle. The working follows the supplied example at lines 757–767 and image69.

x² = 32400 + 14400 − 43200(−1/2) = 68400. Thus x = 261.533936… m, rounding to 262 m. The diagram has the correct 180:120 side ratio and 120° included angle. This adapts the paddock problem at lines 832–836.

HJ² = 81 + 144 − 216(1/2) = 117. Using HJ = √117 = 10.816653… cm gives P = 9 + 12 + √117 = 31.816653… cm ≈ 31.8 cm. The diagram correctly represents GH = 9 cm, GJ = 12 cm and angle HGJ = 60°. This adapts the perimeter exercise at lines 825–830 and image76.
